title: U.S. House · Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District
area: Western Wisconsin, including Eau Claire and La Crosse.

context.text: Incumbent Derrick Van Orden (R) advanced unopposed from the Republican primary. Rebecca Cooke defeated Emily Berge 60.0%-39.9% in the Democratic primary. Two independents, Alexander Valiensi Kent and Rustin Provance, also qualified for the general-election ballot; a third independent, Jayte Welch, withdrew or was disqualified.

candidates.name: Derrick Van Orden
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District (since 2023)

summary.text: Derrick Van Orden is the Republican incumbent representing Wisconsin's 3rd District since 2023. A Navy SEAL who retired as a Senior Chief after 26 years of service, he later worked as an actor and author, reopened the Butternut Cafe with his wife, and won the seat in 2022 after an unsuccessful 2020 run. He serves on the Agriculture, Veterans' Affairs and Armed Services committees and is seeking a third term.

background.text: Born September 15, 1969, in Hennepin County, Minnesota; according to Wikipedia, his family lived in Hartland, Wisconsin, before moving to the Portland, Oregon, area, where he attended Lakeridge High School. His campaign website says he was raised in rural poverty by his mother.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Excelsior University. His campaign website says he later attended law school.

Joined the U.S. Navy in 1988 and served 26 years, retiring in 2014 as a Navy SEAL Senior Chief with multiple combat tours; his official biography lists service in the Horn of Africa, Asia, Europe, and South and Central America, and says he planned Special Operations contingency operations for Europe during a 2012 tour.

After the Navy, appeared in the 2012 film Act of Valor and in two later films, and wrote the book A Book of Man: A Navy SEAL's Guide to the Lost Art of Manhood, according to his campaign website. It also says he consulted with Fortune 500 companies.

Owned and operated the Butternut Cafe in Butternut, Wisconsin, with his wife, Sara Jane, from 2017 to early 2019, according to Wikipedia; his campaign website describes reopening the village cafe after they retired to their farm.
Ran for Wisconsin's 3rd District in 2020 and lost the general election to Democratic incumbent Ron Kind, with 48.6% of the vote.
Elected to the U.S. House in November 2022, defeating Democrat Brad Pfaff 51.8% to 48.1% in the open-seat race to succeed Kind, and took office in January 2023.
Won re-election in 2024, defeating Democrat Rebecca Cooke 51.3% to 48.6%, and advanced unopposed from the August 2026 Republican primary.

Serves on the House Veterans' Affairs Committee (chairman of the Economic Opportunity Subcommittee), the Agriculture Committee (Nutrition, Foreign Agriculture, and Horticulture; Livestock, Dairy, and Poultry) and the Armed Services Committee (Intelligence and Special Operations; Strategic Forces).
His official biography says he and his wife, Sara Jane, live in Wisconsin and have four children and eleven grandchildren; his campaign website gives the grandchild count as 13.

priorities.text: Says he is committed to ensuring western Wisconsin has access to safe drinking water, well-maintained roads and bridges, and reliable rural broadband, citing funding he secured to address PFAS contamination.
Champions the Working Family Tax Cuts legislation, which he says ensures more of workers' earnings remain in their pockets.
Says he will work to protect individuals with preexisting conditions once Obamacare is repealed and a new system implemented allowing for competition in healthcare.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he supports fully repealing the Affordable Care Act and implementing a new system allowing for competition in healthcare, while protecting people with preexisting conditions; also says he secured $1 billion annually for BadgerCare and increased federal ambulance funding for the district.
Told WEAU in August 2026 that he supports fully funding ICE and CBP and enforcing immigration laws.
positions.quote: I support fully funding ICE and CBP to give the resources they need to secure the border, crack down on cartels and fentanyl trafficking, and enforcing our immigration laws.

positions.summary: In a June 2026 statement on a House-passed War Powers Resolution he said the President acted within constitutional authority on Iran and that limiting the President’s ability to respond restricts the Commander-in-Chief.
positions.quote: The Constitution designates the President as Commander-in-Chief for a reason. President Trump acted fully within its constitutional authority and in accordance with the War Powers Resolution of 1973.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (Nutrition, Foreign Agriculture; Vice Chair of Livestock, Dairy, and Poultry), chairs the Economic Opportunity Subcommittee of the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs, and serves on the House Committee on Armed Services (Intelligence and Special Operations; Strategic Forces) in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Rebecca Cooke
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated Emily Berge 60.0%-39.9% in the Democratic primary.

summary.text: Rebecca Cooke is the Democratic nominee for Wisconsin's 3rd District. Raised on an Eau Claire dairy farm, she worked as a campaign fundraiser and political consultant, opened a home goods store and founded a nonprofit that funds women-owned businesses, and served on the Wisconsin Economic Development Corporation board. This is her third run for the seat; she describes her campaign as focused on health care access and affordability, an economy built for working families, and reproductive health care.

background.text: Born in Eau Claire, Wisconsin (December 21, 1987, per Wikipedia); grew up on a dairy farm (Prairie Belle Holsteins) and showed cattle at county fairs through 4-H, according to her Ballotpedia survey response. Wikipedia describes her as the youngest of three children in a dairy farming family.

Began waitressing at 16 while attending North High School, and earned a bachelor's degree from the University of St. Thomas. She says she worked her way through college with Pell Grants, scholarships, financial aid and multiple jobs.
From 2012 to 2014 she was finance director for four congressional campaigns in four states, according to Wikipedia, and from 2015 to 2021 her consulting firm advised eight political campaigns.
Returned to Eau Claire in 2014 and opened a home goods store, Red's Mercantile, which closed in 2022.
Founded a nonprofit in 2016 that provides start-up capital to women-owned small businesses; KSTP describes it as providing start-up capital to small businesses.

Appointed by Gov. Tony Evers in 2019 to the board of the Wisconsin Economic Development Corporation, where she co-chaired the Entrepreneurship & Innovation Committee and later served as secretary; she resigned in November 2021.

Ran for Wisconsin's 3rd District in 2022, finishing second to Brad Pfaff in the Democratic primary. In 2024 she won the Democratic nomination and lost the general election to Rep. Derrick Van Orden, 48.6% to 51.3%.
Won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary over Emily Berge, 60.0% to 39.9%, and has continued working as a waitress during her campaign, according to KSTP.

priorities.text: Says her top messages are tackling the affordability crisis with better wages and lower taxes for working families, making healthcare more affordable and accessible, and ending what she calls a culture of corruption in Washington.
Says she wants to help families buy their first home by deferring property tax payments for first-time buyers for up to five years.

positions.summary: Campaign site says she would expand Medicare to cover vision, dental and hearing, lower the Medicare eligibility age annually, increase Medicare and Medicaid reimbursement rates for rural hospitals, and provide more tax credits to lower ACA exchange premiums.
Campaign site says she supports raising the federal minimum wage to $15 an hour with a rolling implementation plan starting with large corporations.
positions.quote: Increasing the federal minimum wage to $15 an hour

positions.summary: Campaign priorities call for ending the use of tariffs.
positions.quote: End the use of tariffs that have created trade tensions globally and cut off agricultural marketplaces.

positions.summary: Campaign priorities call for federal investment in wind, solar and hydro energy projects.
positions.quote: Draw federal funds for investment in green energy projects that harness our natural resources like wind, solar and hydro energy.

positions.summary: Campaign site says every person should have the right to make decisions about starting or growing a family and that she would protect reproductive healthcare and keep Planned Parenthood federally funded.
positions.quote: I am a firm believer that every person should have the right to make the best decision for themselves about if, when, and how to start or grow a family, free from political or governmental interference.

positions.summary: Campaign site calls for scrapping the Social Security payroll tax cap so higher earners pay more.
positions.quote: Scrap the cap on Social Security so that higher earners are paying their fair share and keeping the program solvent for all of us.

positions.summary: Campaign priorities call for fully funding law enforcement.
positions.quote: Fully fund law enforcement to keep our communities safe and protect our borders.

candidates.researchNotes: Cooke has not held elected office, so there is no official voting or legislative record.

candidates.name: Alexander Valiensi Kent

summary.text: Alexander Valiensi Kent is an independent candidate for Wisconsin's 3rd District from La Crosse. He has a background in social work and philosophy, wrote a 2024 book on online voting, and describes his campaign as independent, voter-directed and accepting no money from donors.

background.text: Lives in La Crosse, Wisconsin; earned a bachelor's degree from Viterbo University in 2014 and a graduate degree from the University of Chicago in 2016.
Describes his background as social work and philosophy; Ballotpedia lists his profession as social work.
Wrote the book "Voter Directed Democracy," published in 2024, which he describes as a political theory about bringing democratic republicanism online.

priorities.text: Says his campaign supports an online system in which verified voters vote directly on issues ("Voter Directed").
priorities.quote: Voter Directed- our campaign supports of the Online Political Evolution where Verified Voters are empowered to vote on everything.

priorities.text: Says his campaign takes no money from any person or group.
priorities.quote: Zero Money- Our campaign isn't taking any money from anyone or any group.

candidates.researchNotes: Completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; his answers describe a voter-directed-democracy platform and take no stance on the guide's issue statements. No campaign website found.

candidates.name: Rustin Provance

summary.text: Rustin Provance is an independent candidate for Wisconsin's 3rd District. In a 2024 Ballotpedia survey he described himself as a Certified Nursing Assistant who opposes taxation he calls illegal and supports term limits. Little other biographical information is public.

background.text: Born in Cameron, Missouri, according to Ballotpedia.
In a 2024 Ballotpedia survey, described himself as a Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA).
Ballotpedia records him as an independent candidate for this seat in 2022 and 2024 who withdrew before the general election each time; he is on the ballot in 2026.

priorities.text: In a 2024 Ballotpedia survey (his 2026 survey is not completed), said he would serve one term.
priorities.quote: I will ONLY serve one term. After that. I'm done.

priorities.text: In the same 2024 survey, called for ending the Federal Reserve.
priorities.quote: End the privately owned bank that is for profit The Federal Reserve, it sends our hard earned wealth to the IMF.

candidates.researchNotes: Has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 survey; priorities come from his 2024 survey. His campaign website (Wix) has no issue content. No statements on the guide's issues found.
